claims.head: Something has to give
claims.body: The Lightning are one of the league’s best for chance quality, and the Wild are near the top of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Lightning’s chance quality wins out.
claims.call: The Lightning’s chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Wild.
claims.nums: Tampa Bay 5th for chance quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Minnesota 6th for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Lightning for chance quality, the Wild at preventing dangerous shots.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals
check.rule: held if tonight's figure lands on the predicted side of the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Vasilevskiy’s rough record against the Wild is a coincidence
claims.body: Vasilevskiy has been shaky against the Wild since 2023-24, well below his usual. It looks like a pattern, but across three seasons a goalie’s record against one team told us nothing about the next meeting. Expect the usual Vasilevskiy.
claims.nums: 6 starts against Minnesota: .877 save percentage · .913 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Vasilevskiy’s record against the Wild.
claims.call: If Vasilevskiy starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .913 than to his .877 against the Wild.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against Minnesota, 4,587 shots against everyone else

check.rule: held if he starts and his save percentage is closer to his usual than to his record against this team; can't judge if he doesn't start

TBL.head: Tampa Bay starts a half-step ahead
TBL.body: Tampa Bay has had more of the chances over recent games and has home ice. Not by much, though: Minnesota can make it interesting if they pounce on loose pucks.

MIN.head: A slightly uphill night for Minnesota
MIN.body: Tampa Bay has had more of the chances over recent games and has home ice. Minnesota can tip it if they pounce on loose pucks.
